facts.fact: The Tony Blair Institute says the National Health Intelligence Center, launched April 2025, integrates real-time data from hospitals, health centres, supply chains and workforce management, and records now flow directly into it instead of being collated manually by the Ministry of Health.

The Tony Blair Institute says the National Health Intelligence Center integrates real-time data from hospitals, health centres, supply chains, workforce management and other sources across the health system.

KT Press reports that the National Health Intelligence Center centralizes, processes and analyzes health data from hospitals, health centers and community health workers, and in its first year contributed to faster ambulance dispatch and disease surveillance, according to the Ministry of Health.

The Rwanda Biomedical Centre says Pandemic Fund board members were shown, at the National Health Intelligence Center, the integration of laboratory information systems with indicator-based surveillance, with several data streams converging in one platform.

systems.owner: Rwanda Biomedical Centre / Ministry of Health

note: eBuzima is a single EMR; the document lists full interoperability across platforms only as a goal, with no exchange between systems stated.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health says the Health Intelligence Center, launched 3 April 2025, takes in data from DHIS2, the eBuzima and cEMR medical records, CRVS, eLMIS, WelTel, emergency medical services and the health workforce system.

The Ministry of Health says the Health Intelligence Center integrates data from DHIS2, eBuzima, cEMR, CRVS, eLMIS, WelTel, emergency medical services and the health workforce management system, from village level to referral hospitals.

The Global Fund case study says Rwanda's Ministry of Health has made the laboratory information systems, the HMIS and the Reagent Management System interoperable, giving end-to-end visibility across testing, results and stock.
facts.system: Laboratory information systems, HMIS and Reagent Management System

facts.fact: The Global Fund case study says three systems, the laboratory information systems, the HMIS and the Reagent Management System, are interoperable in Rwanda, and that a health information exchange at facility level lets clinicians draw on patients' past encounters.
facts.system: Laboratory information systems, HMIS and Reagent Management System

note: Endorsed AU HIE guidelines without technical infrastructure: policy, no exchange in service.

facts.fact: Ecofin Agency reports that Rwanda's National Health Intelligence Center, launched in April 2025, connects the national health management information system, electronic medical records and civil registration databases in one platform.

Ecofin Agency reports that the National Health Intelligence Center draws data from primary care, disease surveillance, human resources, health financing, supply chains and civil registration, connecting the HMIS, electronic medical records and civil registration databases.

The Global Fund says the eFiche record system is interoperable with the government's eBuzima and with Rwanda's Health Information Exchange, and reports HIV, TB and malaria indicators into national systems.

note: A policy roadmap still being developed through roundtables; no exchange between health systems is stated.
